title: Choose the visual world for guba.dev
question: The roll assigned Silkscreen Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Silkscreen Board
options.lineage: PCB silkscreen on blue solder mask, assembly drawings, ENIG pads
options.thesis: The site is a populated circuit board: every project is a placed component, every link a gold pad, and the joke is printed in silkscreen where engineers actually print jokes.
materials: routed copper traces under the mask
options.viewport: A board outline inset from the viewport edge with fiducials in the corners. Title block top-left reads guba.dev, REV 2026.09; nav sits top-right as off-board connectors J1 PROJECTS, J2 BLOG. Centre-left: PATRICK GHEBA in condensed silkscreen caps at massive scale with designator U1, three compact lines beneath it (Computing Science @ University of Groningen; Absolutely no fucking idea what I'm doing; Groningen, NL). Below the name, an edge-connector row of gold fingers: GITHUB, LINKEDIN, INSTAGRAM. Faint copper traces route across the ground between components; hovering any component lights its net gold.
options.risk: Reads as hardware-nerd if the designators get cute; kept dry, small, and factual it reads as an engineer who labels things properly. Blue on white text at long lengths needs the paper drawing for blog posts.

raised.raise: Fixed footprint grid: nav, title block, and section slots hold the same position on every surface; an empty slot is drawn as an unpopulated footprint, never collapsed.
One strict grid is the whole composition; the type scale is a single ramp from designator to board title, nothing set off-ramp.
Gold appears only on things you can press. One accent that is also the control; nothing decorative wears it.
One large unmarked region of bare mask is held open in the first viewport as the compositional anchor; the name does not fill the frame.
No gray anywhere. White ink at full strength; hierarchy comes from weight and size, never opacity.
One dominant element outranks three compact lines: the name at giant scale, the intro held to three lines beneath it.

options.label: Patch Panel Labels
options.lineage: datacenter cable colour code, Brady label tape, patch-panel port maps, rack-unit rulers
options.thesis: The site as the rack you work in: colour-coded runs, printed label tape on every port, and a port map instead of a nav.
materials: white label tape with black thermal print
options.viewport: A left rail is a rack-unit ruler numbered 1U to 42U; the name is a wide printed label across the top row; each section is a port field where projects are ports with a coloured cable jacket per category (blue personal, yellow university) and a printed label under each. Links are printed tape.
options.risk: Label-tape and industrial signage is a look other brutalist personal sites already wear; distinctive here through the colour code, less so at a glance.

options.label: Seven-Segment Mask
options.lineage: bedside clocks, gas-station price totems, scoreboards
options.thesis: The site as a fixed eight-cell mask where only lit segments change.
options.viewport: Four giant digits and a scoreboard of projects in a rigid cell grid.
options.risk: Prose does not survive a seven-segment alphabet.
options.case: Loses both: recruiters do not identify with a clock, and paragraphs cannot be set in segments.
options.kept: Absence drawn as deliberately as presence: fixed slots, ghosted when empty.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.thesis: The whole page as one monospace glyph grid where density is light.
options.viewport: A live glyph-rendered scene with the name and links inside the same grid.
options.risk: Fake-terminal is the gimmick the brief named.
options.case: Loses both: reads as the hacker-portfolio cliché and hurts scanability for a recruiter.
options.kept: One strict grid as the entire composition; a single type ramp.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: transforming silk cape with hidden drawcord channels
options.thesis: Black silk ground, one gold cord as both accent and control.
options.viewport: A flat black plane that gathers into ribs as you pull one gold cord.
options.risk: A fashion object for a CS student's CV page.
options.case: Loses both: no audience identification, and the transformation metaphor carries none of the product's facts.
options.kept: The accent is the control: gold only on what you can press.

options.label: Accretion Disk
options.lineage: black-hole accretion disk, photon ring, event horizon
options.thesis: Void black with concentric time-dilated rings and a gold photon-ring accent.
options.viewport: Labels orbit the rim of a warped disk; the centre stays unmarked black.
options.risk: A shader spectacle with nothing to say about Patrick.
options.case: Loses both: no audience link and the content has no natural place on a rim.
options.kept: One large unmarked region held open as the compositional anchor.

options.label: Op-Art Repeat
options.thesis: Hard black-and-white wave field, no gray, seam never found.
options.viewport: A continuous flexing wave with controls as amplitude regions.
options.risk: The field fights every line of text laid over it.
options.case: Loses both: a moving wave ground undermines the ten-second recruiter read and says nothing about the person.
options.kept: Total palette commitment: no gray whatsoever, hierarchy from weight and size.

options.label: Illuminated Initial
options.lineage: historiated initial, gold-leaf chamber, marginal vine
options.thesis: One giant initial outranks three lines of compact text; the margin is inhabited.
options.viewport: A red P opens into a gold chamber; the intro sits in three gothic lines beside it.
options.risk: Vellum and gothic bookhand on a datacenter technician's site.
options.case: Loses both: the audience does not identify with a manuscript, and the ornament works against the serious tone asked for.
options.kept: One dominant element at giant scale, the text block held to three compact lines.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark-mode developer portfolio, executed impeccably: hero, muted intro, link chips, project rows.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one-line context, social chips, then a hairline list of projects and posts.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the current site and from most developer portfolios by design.
